brandSpecificPaths.Samsung: Settings → Battery → Background usage limits → Put unused apps to sleep
brandSpecificPaths.Google Pixel: Settings → Battery → Battery Saver & Adaptive Battery
brandSpecificPaths.OnePlus: Settings → Battery → More settings → App battery management
brandSpecificPaths.Xiaomi: Settings → Battery & performance → App battery saver
brandSpecificPaths.Motorola: Settings → Battery → Adaptive Battery & Background restrictions

safeSteps.title: Analyze and Limit Background App Drain
safeSteps.action: Inspect Battery Usage in device settings. Identify apps consuming over 5% on standby and restrict their background execution.
safeSteps.rationale: Unoptimized third-party background wake-locks are the primary cause of sudden standby discharge.

safeSteps.title: Adjust Display Refresh Rate and Always-On Display
safeSteps.action: Switch screen refresh rate from dynamic 120Hz to Standard 60Hz and disable Always-On Display (AOD) for 24 hours.
safeSteps.rationale: High refresh rate panels and ambient displays continuously consume 15-25% more GPU power.

safeSteps.title: Clear Google Play Services Cache and Restart
safeSteps.action: Go to Settings → Apps → Google Play Services → Storage → Clear Cache. Then perform a full device reboot.
safeSteps.rationale: Google Play Services sync loops can lock background CPU states, causing severe battery drain.

safetyEscalation.advice: WARNING: Physical battery swelling or burning odor indicates a serious chemical hazard. Stop using the device immediately, do not charge it, and take it to an authorized brand repair center.

categories.name: Phone overheating
symptoms: Device becomes hot to touch during basic tasks
Camera app closes due to temperature warning

brandSpecificPaths.Samsung: Settings → Device Care → Optimization & Performance profile → Light mode
brandSpecificPaths.Google Pixel: Settings → System → System updates & Settings → Battery → Battery Share (turn off)
brandSpecificPaths.Xiaomi: Settings → Battery → Battery protection & Clear background cache when locked

safeSteps.title: Isolate Heavy Background Tasks and Remove Insulating Cases
safeSteps.action: Remove thick rubber/leather protective cases and close resource-intensive games or camera applications.
safeSteps.rationale: Thick cases trap heat against the phone frame, preventing passive aluminum/glass dissipation.

safeSteps.title: Enable Light Performance Mode & Disable 5G Search
safeSteps.action: Navigate to Performance/Battery settings and switch from Maximum to Standard or Light performance profile. Turn off 5G if signal is weak.
safeSteps.rationale: Continuous searching for weak 5G signals drives the RF modem at maximum power, generating excessive heat.

safeSteps.title: Boot in Safe Mode to Rule Out Malicious Background Apps
safeSteps.action: Press and hold Power Off on the power menu until 'Safe Mode' appears. Tap to restart into Safe Mode and test temperature for 2 hours.
safeSteps.rationale: Safe Mode disables all third-party apps, confirming whether overheating is caused by third-party malware/bugs.

safetyEscalation.advice: Unplug the phone immediately. Place it on a non-flammable surface and bring it to an authorized technician.

brandSpecificPaths.Samsung: Settings → General management → Reset → Reset Wi-Fi and Bluetooth settings
brandSpecificPaths.Google Pixel: Settings → System → Reset options → Reset Wi-Fi, mobile & Bluetooth
brandSpecificPaths.OnePlus: Settings → System settings → Back up and reset → Reset phone → Reset network settings
brandSpecificPaths.Xiaomi: Settings → Connection & sharing → Reset Wi-Fi, mobile networks and Bluetooth
brandSpecificPaths.Motorola: Settings → System → Reset options → Reset Wi-Fi, mobile & Bluetooth

safeSteps.title: Forget Network and Toggle Airplane Mode
safeSteps.action: Go to Settings → Wi-Fi, tap the gear icon next to your network, tap Forget. Turn Airplane mode ON for 10 seconds, turn OFF, and reconnect.
safeSteps.rationale: Forces the network stack to renew DHCP leases and clear stale DNS cache.

safeSteps.title: Disable MAC Randomization and Private DNS
safeSteps.action: In Wi-Fi network settings, change 'MAC Address Type' from Randomized to Phone MAC. Go to Settings → Connections → Private DNS and select Automatic.
safeSteps.rationale: Some home and university routers reject frequently cycling randomized MAC addresses or custom DNS resolvers.

safeSteps.title: Reset Network Settings
safeSteps.action: Navigate to System/General Management → Reset → Reset Network Settings. (Note: Saved Wi-Fi passwords will be cleared).
safeSteps.rationale: Clears corrupted network configuration files without erasing any personal photos or app data.

triggers: wi-fi toggle completely greyed out after network reset and factory reboot
safetyEscalation.advice: A permanently greyed-out Wi-Fi toggle after network reset indicates a failing Wi-Fi/Bluetooth IC chip. Visit an authorized repair center.

categories.name: Mobile network problems
symptoms: No Service or Emergency Calls Only

brandSpecificPaths.Samsung: Settings → Connections → Mobile networks → Network mode (LTE/3G/2G auto)
brandSpecificPaths.Google Pixel: Settings → Network & internet → SIMs → Preferred network type
brandSpecificPaths.OnePlus: Settings → Mobile network → Select SIM → Preferred network type
brandSpecificPaths.Xiaomi: Settings → SIM cards & mobile networks → Select SIM → Preferred network type
brandSpecificPaths.Motorola: Settings → Network & internet → Mobile network → Preferred network type

safeSteps.title: Toggle Airplane Mode & Re-seat Physical SIM / Toggle eSIM
safeSteps.action: Turn Airplane Mode ON for 15 seconds then OFF. If using a physical SIM card, gently eject, inspect for dust, and re-insert.
safeSteps.rationale: Re-initiates the baseband handshake with nearest telecom cellular towers.

safeSteps.title: Switch Preferred Network Type to LTE / 4G
safeSteps.action: Go to Settings → Mobile Networks → Preferred network type and choose LTE/4G Auto instead of 5G Auto.
safeSteps.rationale: In areas with sparse 5G coverage, continuous 5G/LTE handoff can drop calls and freeze mobile data.

safeSteps.title: Reset Access Point Names (APN) to Default
safeSteps.action: Go to Mobile Networks → Access Point Names (APN) → Tap three dots in upper corner → Reset to default.
safeSteps.rationale: Restores original carrier cellular data and MMS gateway configurations.

safetyEscalation.advice: If the IMEI or Baseband version shows 'Unknown' in About Phone, the cellular modem module is damaged. Contact authorized brand service.

brandSpecificPaths.Samsung: Settings → Battery → Charging settings → Fast charging toggle
brandSpecificPaths.OnePlus: Settings → Battery → Wise Charging / SuperVOOC toggle

safeSteps.title: Inspect and Clean the USB-C Port Gently
safeSteps.action: Use a wooden or plastic toothpick under good lighting to gently clear pocket lint from the USB-C port. Never use metal pins.
safeSteps.rationale: Compressed pocket lint prevents the charging cable pins from making full physical contact with the charging port.

safeSteps.title: Test with an Alternative Official Cable & Power Brick
safeSteps.action: Test charging using a known working certified original cable and wall adapter plugged into a different wall socket.
safeSteps.rationale: Over 70% of intermittent charging issues stem from internal wire fractures in worn charging cables.

safeSteps.title: Clear USB Settings System App Cache
safeSteps.action: Go to Settings → Apps → Enable 'Show system apps' → Select USBSettings → Storage → Clear Data / Cache. Restart device.
safeSteps.rationale: Clears false-positive 'Moisture Detected' alerts after the port has already dried thoroughly.

safetyEscalation.advice: DANGER: Do not attempt to charge a phone with charred or smoking port pins. Disconnect immediately and take to an authorized technician.

categories.name: Camera problems
symptoms: Camera app crashes on launch (Camera Error)
Photos blurry or unable to focus

brandSpecificPaths.Samsung: Settings → Apps → Camera → Storage → Clear cache & Clear data
brandSpecificPaths.Google Pixel: Settings → Apps → Pixel Camera → Storage & cache → Clear storage
brandSpecificPaths.OnePlus: Settings → Apps → App management → Camera → Storage usage → Clear data
brandSpecificPaths.Xiaomi: Settings → Apps → Manage apps → Camera → Clear data
brandSpecificPaths.Motorola: Settings → Apps → Camera → Storage & cache → Clear storage

safeSteps.title: Force Stop and Clear Camera App Data
safeSteps.action: Navigate to Settings → Apps → Camera. Tap 'Force Stop', then go to Storage and tap 'Clear Data'. (Photos in gallery are safe and not deleted).
safeSteps.rationale: Clears corrupted camera preferences, lens profiles, and temporary HDR image buffers.

safeSteps.title: Clean Lens Surface & Revoke Third-Party Camera Permissions
safeSteps.action: Clean camera lens with a microfiber cloth. Go to Settings → Privacy → Permission manager → Camera, and revoke camera access from untrusted apps.
safeSteps.rationale: Background apps locking the camera hardware interface can prevent the main camera app from accessing the sensor.

safeSteps.title: Test Camera in Safe Mode
safeSteps.action: Restart into Safe Mode to determine whether third-party social media camera filters are causing system sensor driver crashes.
safeSteps.rationale: Isolates operating system camera drivers from conflicting third-party video apps.

safetyEscalation.advice: Cracked lenses or physically broken optical image stabilization (OIS) motors require sensor module replacement at an authorized service center.

categories.name: Storage problems
symptoms: System sluggish due to low free memory

brandSpecificPaths.Samsung: Settings → Device care → Storage → Recycle bin & Duplicate files
brandSpecificPaths.Google Pixel: Settings → Storage → Free up space (Files by Google)
brandSpecificPaths.Xiaomi: Settings → About phone → Storage → Deep clean

safeSteps.title: Clear App Caches and Empty System Recycle Bins
safeSteps.action: Open Device Care / Storage. Check Gallery Trash/Recycle Bin and Files Trash and tap 'Empty'.
safeSteps.rationale: Deleted photos and videos remain in the trash bin for 30 days by default, consuming gigabytes of active storage.

safeSteps.title: Clear Messaging App Media and Large Downloads
safeSteps.action: Open messaging apps (WhatsApp, Telegram) → Settings → Storage and data → Manage storage. Delete forwarded video archives.
safeSteps.rationale: Chat apps accumulate heavy video databases that do not automatically appear in standard photo galleries.

safeSteps.title: Uninstall Unused Heavy Apps & Offload to Cloud
safeSteps.action: Review apps larger than 1GB that have not been opened in 30 days and uninstall them. Backup photos to Google Photos/OneDrive.
safeSteps.rationale: Android requires at least 10-15% free internal storage for virtual RAM paging and database indexing.

safetyEscalation.advice: If storage fails to format or displays I/O read-only errors, the internal flash storage chip is degrading. Backup data and contact service.

categories.name: Phone lagging
symptoms: UI stutters when scrolling or opening apps
Apps take multiple seconds to launch

brandSpecificPaths.Samsung: Settings → Device care → Auto optimization → Auto restart
brandSpecificPaths.Google Pixel: Settings → System → Developer options → Window animation scale

safeSteps.title: Reboot Device & Close Inactive Background Apps
safeSteps.action: Perform a complete device restart. Check recent apps screen and close heavy tasks.
safeSteps.rationale: Rebooting clears volatile RAM, terminates zombie system processes, and flushes kernel buffer memory.

safeSteps.title: Adjust Window Animation Scales to 0.5x
safeSteps.action: Enable Developer Options (tap Build Number 7 times). In Developer Options, change Window, Transition, and Animator scales from 1.0x to 0.5x.
safeSteps.rationale: Halves the visual rendering duration for window transitions, making the user interface respond twice as quickly.

safeSteps.title: Wipe System Cache Partition from Android Recovery
safeSteps.action: Power off. Hold Power + Volume Up until the recovery screen appears. Use volume keys to select 'Wipe Cache Partition' and confirm.
safeSteps.rationale: Clears obsolete compiled Dalvik/ART runtime cache files left behind by OS updates without deleting user data.

safetyEscalation.advice: Continuous bootloops or kernel panics after factory reset indicate motherboard or processor failure. Visit an authorized brand service center.
